Knowledge recorded by Shinnecock elders in 2014

Cattails

Cattails were sewn into dwelling coverings and woven into baskets and carrying bags. The catalogue also records food, medicinal, and personal-care uses. These accounts show how wetland plants supported many aspects of household life.1

Places named in the catalogue

Cold Springs; The Neck / Riverhead; Stony Brook; Watermill; Montauk; Napeague.1

Page references

The Shinnecock Environmental Department compiled this catalogue from elders’ memories and community resource knowledge in 2014. Food and medicine appear here as historical knowledge; safe identification and treatment require current guidance.

Shinnecock Environmental Department, Natural Resources Identified by Shinnecock Elders, April 4, 2014, PDF p. 7. Page numbers count the cover as PDF page 1.
